tier_reason: PR #23 (merged 2026-10-05) states 'bm3dcuda on the same harness: 636 fps; this branch 732 fps at the default 3 streams' on an RTX 5080 at 1080p, and docs/api/bm3d.md adds first-party ratios against bm3dcuda (measured 2026-10-06); no timing harness is in the repo (tests/cuda_compare.py compares bm3dcuda PSNR only, tests/cuda/stress_cuda.py is a memory soak), and host CPU, driver, bm3dcuda build and bm3dcuda parameters are unstated, so first-party without methodology: C.

corrections.workload: nss_cuda.BM3D at its default shape (block 8, group 8, sigma 3) on 1080p Gray float clips, 3 streams (the default at the time of PR #23; the current docs/api/bm3d.md gives num_streams default 1), RTX 5080, source frames served from VapourSynth's cache, A and B alternated, kernel times from Nsight Systems; bm3dcuda 'on the same harness'. The repo's docs/api/bm3d.md adds first-party figures for 1080p GRAYS, RTX 5080, one stream, measured 2026-10-06 against bm3dcuda with the same search: about 1.25x spatial with 32 VapourSynth threads (bounded by frame transfers; the kernels take the same time), rolling temporal 2.7x at radius 1 and 3.3x at radius 2 with 32 threads (1.4x with one thread; random access 1.15x with one thread and 2.2x with 32), and chroma=1 at YUV444 243, 238 and 229 fps (spatial, radius 1, radius 2) against bm3dcuda chroma=True 200, 94 and 65 fps.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers in a PR body and in docs/api/bm3d.md; the timing harness that produced the 636 fps bm3dcuda figure is not in the repo (tests/cuda_compare.py runs bm3dcuda only for a clean-PSNR column, tests/cuda/stress_cuda.py is a device-memory soak, the tests/bench_*.cpp files are CPU benchmarks, tools/ holds only a codelet generator), and host CPU, driver, bm3dcuda build (cuda or rtc variant) and bm3dcuda parameters are not stated, so tier C. The gain over bm3dcuda is modest at the default (about 1.15x, derived from page data) and the docs say the spatial case is bound by frame transfers while the kernels take the same time as bm3dcuda, so the spatial win comes from host-side pipelining rather than faster GPU work; the larger 2.7x and 3.3x wins are for the rolling temporal mode with 32 threads, which keeps the temporal sums on the device while bm3dcuda returns a fat intermediate for a separate aggregation step. The 732 fps bm3dcuda-comparison figure does not match the PR's own Gray sigma 3 after-figure (710 fps), so it was a separate run; the PR also reports its own before/after (478 to 710 fps Gray, 1.49x), so the bm3dcuda gap is recent: it was produced by PR #23, merged 2026-10-05. The stream default has since changed from 3 to 1 and the README now quotes about 790 fps for 1080p BM3D with one or three streams, with no bm3dcuda figure beside it. The 'final=1' gains (303 to 730 fps and so on) are against the plugin's own two-call form, not bm3dcuda. Repository is days old in its visible history (first visible commit 2026-10-04, 131 commits) and the README says the project is WIP and still calls CUDA a 'future route' although the CUDA plugin is documented, so numbers may change quickly. PSNR on its worst case improved from 73.5 to 138.9 dB after PR #23, so earlier output had larger numeric error; CUDA output is not bit-identical to the CPU plugin (60 dB gate). GPL-2.0-only per the CMakeLists SPDX header; the FFTW-generated DCT codelets are GPL-2.0-or-later.

notes: All PR #23 numbers (636 vs 732 fps, 478 to 710, 354 to 438, 344 to 450, PSNR 73.5 to 138.9 dB) and the docs/api/bm3d.md ratios appear as recorded. Shortcomings: first-party, no timing harness in the repo, CPU/driver/bm3dcuda build unstated, spatial gain from transfers not kernels, 1 star, WIP repo days old, stream default changed after the measurement.
